local.area: Colorado Springs, CO (with Denver metro ~70 mi north as the higher-value / show destination)
noFeeReality: A local pickup + cash handoff = 0% fees on every platform. Fees only appear when you ship. This is the single biggest lever for a Colorado Springs seller.
Facebook Marketplace and OfferUp are the only two with a true 0% on local pickup + cash. List as 'local pickup only / cash'.
Mercari 'Local' is NOT fee-free — even after Mercari dropped its separate payment fee (Jan 6, 2026), the 10% sell fee still applies to local. Worse than OfferUp/FB for local. (Verified)
Craigslist is 0% to list most items, all cash, but no buyer protection — meet in a safe zone.
Whatnot (~11% all-in: 8% sell + ~2.9% + $0.30) is a ship-based reach/velocity play, not a local-cash play.
Selling to a shop counter or consigning trades a 20-50% haircut for convenience and reach; local + cash keeps everything but you do the legwork.

safeSpots: CSPD Sand Creek Police Substation — designated safe-exchange alcove built specifically for online-transaction meetups, in the lobby across from a 24/7-staffed front desk, with cameras throughout. This is THE named CSPD safe-exchange location. (Verified — Gazette + KRDO.) Confirm current address/hours via CSPD non-emergency 719-444-7000 — station addresses occasionally change (est.).
Any CSPD station lobby can be used per CSPD's own guidance — pick the one nearest you. (Verified)

Standard safe-deal practice: meet in daylight at the police lot or a busy lit store entrance; bring a buddy; count cash on the spot; for higher-value cards verify authenticity before money changes hands; cash only (no Zelle/Venmo 'oops' reversals, no checks); don't give your home address — 'local pickup' should mean a public meet, not your porch, for anything valuable.

byValueTier.advice: Don't ship — fees and time eat it. Trade in at a local shop for STORE CREDIT (Unbound, Card Cosmos, or Hite's — credit ~70-80% of market beats ~50% cash; %s are estimates, confirm in person), or list a LOT on Facebook Marketplace / OfferUp for local cash at 0% fee. Bulk commons -> just take store credit at any of the three. Benchmark a 'fair' shop offer against MeH's posted 60% credit / 40% cash.

Facebook Marketplace or OfferUp, LOCAL PICKUP + CASH, meet at the Sand Creek CSPD safe-exchange zone. Keeps 100% vs ~50-60% at a shop counter and vs ~10-13% in shipping fees. Use the Hite's Pokemon group to find a buyer fast.

Two strong paths. (1) Sell to competing dealers in person at a Denver Card Show (free entry; Feb 27-Mar 1 and June 26-28, 2026) — multiple dealers under one roof = better offers + immediate cash. (2) Consign or sell to Impact Sports Cards (Springs) — they specialize in vintage WOTC + graded, do consignment, and buy collections; trade a cut for reach and not having to find a buyer. For raw vintage that might grade well, get it authenticated/graded first.

ebayApi: Create AND publish a live eBay listing programmatically — no form, no browser — via Trading AddItem/AddFixedPriceItem (one call) or Sell Inventory API's createOrReplaceInventoryItem -> createOffer -> publishOffer (better for bulk). (Verified)

Programmatic photo upload: Trading UploadSiteHostedPictures pushes binary images to eBay Picture Services (EPS) and returns HTTPS URLs to attach. Inventory API instead takes imageUrls that must already be public HTTPS. Rules: up to 24 images, min 500px (1000px+ recommended), all HTTPS, and you can't mix self-hosted + EPS URLs in one listing. (Verified)
Bulk-list many cards in a batch; auto price/quantity/relist updates; and pull sold/active data back into the app. (Verified)
Catalog match for set/number item-specifics where eBay has the card in its catalog. (Verified)

Setup bar the user must clear once (BYOK dev account): join eBay Developers Program (free, ~1 business day approval (est.)); create Sandbox + Production app keysets (App ID/Cert ID/Dev ID); get a USER OAuth token via the authorization-code grant flow with scope sell.inventory (plus refresh-token handling); and opt into Business Policies with payment + fulfillment + return policies created — every Inventory offer requires all three, and this is the step that trips people up. (Verified)

Effort to wire up: a real coding project (OAuth dance + token refresh, business-policy setup, XML or JSON request bodies, image hosting/upload, category + item-specifics mapping) — roughly a weekend-to-a-week for someone comfortable with code, or wrapped once in a BYOK helper and reused (est.). Not click-and-go.

Note on URL prefill: eBay's quick-list now starts at a prelist suggestion page (ebay.com/sl/prelist/suggest) that keyword/catalog-matches what you type — it is a keyword nudge, NOT a documented title/price/description prefill query-string. There is no official URL scheme to one-shot-prefill the full Sell-Your-Item form; true prefill only exists via the API. (est. on absence — no documented param found)
fbReality: There is NO public Facebook Marketplace API to read or create personal P2P listings, and NO URL-parameter prefill for the create-listing form. Marketplace create is manual entry / copy-paste only. Every developer-facing source 2019->2026 reaches the same conclusion. (Verified)

Meta's Commerce Platform / Catalog API / Commerce Manager covers BUSINESS Shops (catalog-backed Facebook/Instagram storefronts, often Shopify-synced) — it does NOT put your card on personal peer-to-peer Marketplace. Different surface, different product. (Verified)

The 'Marketplace Partner Item/Seller API' and 'Marketplace Approval API' exist but are closed, approved-partner-only programs (large auto/retail/inventory partners) — an individual reseller cannot sign up. (Verified docs exist; est. on accessibility)

So the realistic ceiling on Facebook is 'prep-and-hand-off': the app copies the title to clipboard, copies the description, stages your actual photo files in a folder, and OPENS the create form — then YOU paste, drag the photos, and hit submit. This removes ~80% of the typing while keeping you the human doing the final action.

Auto-posting via browser puppetry (what some cross-listers do for FB) is against Facebook's automation ToS and carries real Marketplace-ban / shadow-ban risk if it looks bot-like (volume, speed, patterns). The prep-and-open-form assist is the ToS-safe, ban-resistant version. (Verified risk; est. on exact thresholds)

Architecture takeaway: same card record feeds both channels — eBay = real API automation (worth the one-time setup), Facebook = prep-and-open-form assist (the only thing legally/technically possible).

crossListTools.price: ~$8.99/mo entry; realistically $20-$70/mo plus $5-$12 add-ons for useful features.

crossListTools.name: List Perfectly
crossListTools.how: Opens multiple browser tabs per platform; you often finish/publish each form manually. Cross-posts to ~10 platforms incl. FB Marketplace + eBay. (Its FB behavior IS the 'prep-and-open-form' pattern this app should mirror.)

crossListTools.name: Crosslist
crossListTools.how: API-first when the marketplace supports it (e.g. eBay = clean API), falls back to a secure local browser extension when no API exists (e.g. Facebook). Covers eBay + FB Marketplace among others. This is the cleanest model of the 'eBay-API + FB-puppetry' split.

crossListTools.name: Zentail
crossListTools.how: Mid/enterprise multichannel commerce/PIM (Amazon, Walmart, eBay, Shopify via real APIs/feeds). Does NOT do personal Facebook Marketplace P2P — overkill and wrong-shaped for a single card seller. (est. on fit)
crossListTools.price: Enterprise pricing — not appropriate for a cards-only/low-volume seller.

photoPolicy: eBay's Images/videos/text policy (id=4240) is the governing rule: sellers should write their own text and take their own photos. (Verified)
USED items REQUIRE a photo of the actual item — stock images are prohibited as the main photo on used items. (Verified)

You may NOT use images from a manufacturer's website, Google Images, or another eBay listing / another seller / another website, even if publicly visible — that's copyright infringement, removable via VeRO (Verified Rights Owner), and can get your account sanctioned. (Verified)

Raw singles (used/ungraded) = the 'used item, actual photo' case: photograph YOUR actual card, front and back. A catalog/stock image of 'that card' doesn't represent your card's surface, centering, whitening — and using one both violates policy and misrepresents condition (-> buyer disputes). (Verified principle)

Graded slabs (PSA/CGC/BGS/SGC): photograph the ACTUAL slab, showing the grading company's label/logo and the cert number clearly through the case. eBay's Authenticity Guarantee for trading cards re-verifies the physical slab matches the listing, so a real slab photo is effectively required. (Verified)

Sealed product (booster boxes/ETBs, factory sealed = 'new'): catalog/manufacturer stock images CAN be acceptable when matched to eBay's catalog or with manufacturer permission — but you're still safer including an actual photo, and any seal damage must be shown. (Verified for catalog/permission cases; est. on 'also show actual')

eBay catalog images are sharable by all sellers ONLY when your item is matched to eBay's product catalog — that is the one legitimate 'stock photo' path, and it's eBay-provided, not grabbed from elsewhere. (Verified)

Facebook applies the same principle: your listing images should be your own photos / images you have rights to. There is no 'use a card stock image' carve-out for personal Marketplace. (Verified general FB IP policy; est. that cards follow the same rule)
imageGuidance: HONEST default the app should enforce: raw singles and graded slabs REQUIRE the user's own photo of the actual card/slab (front and back; slab shows label + cert #). Don't auto-fill a listing image from any Google/stock/other-seller source — that's a copyright + policy problem and misrepresents condition.

Catalog/stock images are a REFERENCE ONLY in-app (to help identify the card / autofill set + number + name), never the listing photo for a raw single or slab. The only time a stock/catalog image is OK as the actual listing image is sealed product matched to eBay's catalog or with manufacturer permission, or an eBay catalog-matched item.

Fast, repeatable photo workflow to bake into the app: phone + good diffuse light, plain/neutral background, card flat or in a stand, front and back, shot square-on to avoid glare on slabs/sleeves; angle raw cards slightly to reveal surface/whitening. (Verified eBay photo tips)
Use eBay's built-in AI background removal / 'Background enhancement' (in-app, iOS, US/UK/DE, rolling to Android) — free studio-look cleanup. Off-app, Photoroom or Simplified do the same. (Verified)

A small repeatable rig — phone clamp + fixed overhead copy-stand position + two soft lights or a lightbox — gives an identical top-down shot for every card so bulk photography is fast. NOTE: a specific product named 'GradeStage' could NOT be verified (no such product surfaced) — treat it as a generic copy-stand/lightbox concept, not a confirmed brand. (est./unverified)

The app should store the user's actual photos named per card in a folder ready to drag-drop into either listing form, so the same real images feed both the eBay API upload and the Facebook manual attach.
smoothestFlow: Per card, the app preps everything up to the human submit: (1) prefilled title copied to clipboard (e.g. 'Charizard ex 199/165 SV151 PSA 10 — Holo Pokemon'); (2) copied description (condition, set, number, grade, cert #); (3) the user's actual photo(s) named per card, staged in a folder; (4) opens the create form (FB Marketplace Create > Item; eBay sl/prelist/suggest).

On Facebook this prep-and-open-form assist IS the realistic ceiling — full stop. You paste, drag photos, hit submit. It removes ~80% of the typing and is ToS-safe because YOU are the human doing the final action. (This mirrors what List Perfectly does for FB.)

On eBay, the same card record can go two ways: today, the same prep-and-open-form assist; OR, once the user does the BYOK dev-account setup, flip to full API automation — one-click create + publish via AddFixedPriceItem or Inventory createOffer/publishOffer, programmatic photo upload (UploadSiteHostedPictures -> EPS), batch listing, and auto price/relist + sold/active sync.

Right architecture for the BYOK app: eBay = real API automation (worth the one-time setup), Facebook = prep-and-open-form assist (the only thing possible). One card record feeds both — never duplicate data entry.

Honesty guardrail to surface in the UI: never auto-attach a non-owned image; require the user's own actual photo for raw singles and slabs; reserve catalog/stock images for identification/autofill and for the narrow sealed/catalog-matched cases where they're allowed.
